headline: Chittagong Port cargo movement halts after alleged assault on union leaders
summary: Transport workers suspended operations at Chittagong Port protesting the alleged physical assault of two union leaders by port security staff. The incident stemmed from disputes over inflated entry fees.
details: Cargo and container movement through the gates of Chittagong Port was brought to a standstill this afternoon by transport workers. They are protesting the alleged assault of two union leaders by the port's security staff, which began around 3:00 PM.

The dispute reportedly escalated when security guards assaulted Moktar Hossain, treasurer of the Chattogram District Prime Mover Trailer, Concrete Mixer, Flatbed, Dump Truck Workers Union, as he attempted to record the collection of extra money at Gate No 5. The actual port entry fee is Tk 57.50, but security staff have allegedly been collecting Tk 80 to Tk 90.

Following the incident, Hasan Mahmud, joint secretary of the same union, along with other leaders, was allegedly confined and assaulted by approximately 200 security staff members when they went to attend a meeting at the Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) Security department.

In response to the alleged assaults, prime mover and other transport workers halted cargo and container transport through several gates from 4:30 PM. Off-dock operators confirmed that the transport of containers between the port and 21 private off-docks remained suspended until 8:00 PM.

CPA Secretary Syed Refayet Hamim acknowledged that cargo transport through two gates was suspended. He stated that the authority has initiated efforts to resolve the issue, with senior CPA officials meeting with leaders of various transport owners' and workers' associations in the evening.
caption:

headline_marked: [[17 crude bombs]] found at old trade fair ground in Dhaka, defused by SRB
headline: 17 crude bombs found at old trade fair ground in Dhaka, defused by SRB
summary: Explosives including petrol bombs were recovered and safely defused by the Special Response Battalion during an afternoon operation. The area was secured following a tip-off.
details: Seventeen crude bombs and two petrol bombs were recovered from the old trade fair ground in Dhaka’s Sher-e-Bangla Nagar. The Special Response Battalion (SRB) conducted the operation in the afternoon after receiving a tip-off.

The SRB's bomb disposal unit successfully recovered, scanned, and defused all the explosives found at the site. Squadron Leader Nifaz Rahman of SRB-2 confirmed the successful operation to The Daily Star.
